features.name: Calls Dashboard
features.does: Shows phone call volume, duration, live calls and calls with issues, with a table linking each call (From, To, Direction, Status) to its session.
features.value: Phone operations in the same place as agent quality: from a call record straight into what the agent did.
features.say: Every phone call in and out shows up here, with any call that had problems flagged, and each one links to the full session with the agent.
features.ask: Roughly how many calls a day does your team handle today, and what share could an agent fully resolve?
features.limits: demo-tour has no calls yet (empty table).
features.ask_technical: Inbound, outbound, or both, and what peak concurrency do you expect?

features.name: LiveKit Phone Numbers
features.does: Rent US local or toll-free numbers directly in LiveKit and route them to agents with no third-party SIP trunk.
features.value: Zero to a ringing agent in about a minute, one vendor and one bill, fewer network hops for better audio.
features.say: You can get a phone number right here, no phone carrier account or trunk setup, and point it at your agent in about a minute. Every plan includes one free US number.
features.ask: Do your callers reach you on numbers you already own, or would new numbers work for a pilot?
features.limits: US only; inbound only for now (outbound coming); call forwarding via TransferSIPParticipant not yet supported; released numbers billed for the full month.
features.ask_technical: Do you need outbound dialing or non-US numbers? If so we'd use a SIP trunk from your carrier.

features.name: Number Routing (Configure number)
features.does: From a number's menu, attach it to an existing dispatch rule or create a new one, which decides which agent answers.
features.value: Change which agent answers a number in seconds, without touching the carrier.
features.say: Each number is attached to a routing rule, so switching which agent answers is a dropdown, not a ticket with your phone provider.
features.ask: Do different numbers or departments need different agents, like sales versus support?
use_cases: Swapping in a new agent version
features.limits: The demo number is 'Not configured' in the table; the dialog shows the 'Route to Agent' rule available.
features.ask_technical: Would you route by called number, by trunk, or by metadata to one generic agent?

features.name: Dispatch Rules
features.does: Decide which room each inbound caller joins and which agent is dispatched: Individual (a room per caller), Direct (one room, optional PIN), Callee (room per called number).
features.value: Callers are isolated in their own room with the right agent, automatically, at any scale.
features.say: A dispatch rule is the switchboard: when a call comes in, it gives the caller their own private room and sends in the right agent.
features.ask: When a call comes in, what decides who should answer it today: the number dialed, the time of day, the caller?
features.limits: Reuse rules across calls (don't create one per call). Individual rules put the caller's number in the room name, which PII redaction does not remove.
features.ask_technical: Do you need custom participant attributes or metadata on callers (JSON editor only)?

features.name: Agent Dispatch on Calls
features.does: Names the agent that joins each call, which deployment (production or a non-production one) and passes dispatch metadata as job metadata.
features.value: One agent build can serve many lines and customers, configured per number with metadata.
features.say: Here you pick which agent answers, and you can pass context like which brand or clinic the number belongs to, so one agent serves many lines.
features.ask: Would the same agent answer for several brands or locations, just with different details?
features.limits: Agent must be registered with that agent name (explicit dispatch).
features.source: live dashboard (verified Add agent fields) + docs
features.ask_technical: Would you read ctx.job.metadata to switch data stores or workflows per number?

features.name: Inbound Routing Match
features.does: Limits a dispatch rule to specific numbers or trunks; with none selected it applies to all.
features.value: Precise control over which calls go where as you add numbers and carriers.
features.say: You choose exactly which numbers or carrier connections this rule covers, or leave it open to catch everything.
features.ask: How many phone lines or carriers would feed into this over the next year?
features.limits: Overlapping rules on the same trunk need distinct numbers or PINs.
features.ask_technical: Do you need region-pinned trunks for local telephony regulations?

features.name: JSON Editor
features.does: Edit the full dispatch rule or trunk as JSON, exposing every API parameter (attributes, metadata, PIN, room config).
features.value: Everything in the UI is the same object your code and CLI manage, so you can automate it.
features.say: Everything you click here is plain configuration you can also manage from code or the command line, so nothing is locked in the UI.
features.ask: Would your team set this up by hand, or manage it as code through your deploy pipeline?
features.limits: Some parameters (attributes, metadata) are JSON-editor only.
features.ask_technical: Would you manage trunks and rules via 'lk sip' CLI or the SIP API in CI?

features.name: SIP Trunks (bring your carrier)
features.does: Connect your existing carrier (Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, Exotel, Wavix, Sinch...) or contact center to LiveKit for inbound and outbound calls using your own numbers.
features.value: Keep your numbers and carrier contracts, and add AI agents beside your existing contact center.
features.say: If you already have numbers and a phone carrier, you keep them: you point them at this address and your agent starts answering, no rip-and-replace.
features.ask: Which phone carrier or contact center platform do your calls run through today?
features.limits: Static SIP IP ranges only in some regions; prefer username/password auth on the provider side.
features.ask_technical: Inbound via IP allowlist or digest auth? Any SIP headers you need passed to the agent?

features.name: Trunk Security and Audio Options
features.does: Restrict inbound trunks to trusted IPs and numbers, encrypt media with SRTP, pass SIP headers to the agent, and enable Krisp noise cancellation; outbound trunks use address, transport and credentials.
features.value: Secure, clear calls: only your carrier can reach the agent and background noise is removed before the agent hears it.
features.say: You can lock the line to your carrier only, encrypt the audio, and turn on noise cancellation so the agent hears the caller, not the traffic behind them.
features.ask: Do your callers often call from noisy places like cars or job sites?
features.limits: Empty allowlist or 0.0.0.0/0 allows all IPs.
features.source: live dashboard (verified Inbound and Outbound fields)
features.ask_technical: Do you require SRTP/TLS end to end, and which SIP headers (e.g. X-Customer-ID) should reach the agent?

features.name: Telephony Capabilities and Proof
features.does: DTMF, cold (REFER) and warm transfer to humans, caller ID, HD voice, region pinning, noise cancellation, answering machine detection for outbound, and Connectors for Twilio and WhatsApp without SIP.
features.value: Production telephony features in the same platform as the agent; telli runs 30,000+ calls a day across 400+ SIP trunks on LiveKit.
features.say: It handles the real phone stuff: keypad tones, warm handoff to a person with context, voicemail detection on outbound. telli runs over thirty thousand calls a day across four hundred carrier connections on it.
features.ask: When the agent can't help, how should the caller reach a person: transfer to your queue, or a callback?
features.limits: No SIP REGISTER or video over SIP. Outbound voicemail attempts are still billed.
features.ask_technical: Do you need warm transfer into a specific CCaaS (Genesys, Five9, Twilio Flex) with context passed along?

demo_instructions:
1. Frame it: putting an agent on the phone usually means a carrier account, buying numbers, configuring trunks and wiring SIP before you hear a single ring. Ask: 'How do callers reach you today, and which calls would you want an agent to answer first?' (if technical: 'Which carrier or contact center platform do calls run through today?')
2. Click 'Telephony' in the sidebar: the Calls dashboard (Total calls, Active calls, Calls with issues) sits next to everything else, and each call links to its full agent session. demo-tour has no calls yet; say so in one line.
3. Click 'Phone numbers', then 'Rent a number': numbers by area code, $1 a month, one free US number on every plan. Click 'Close' (never 'Rent').
4. Open the number's menu ('Open menu') > 'Configure with existing dispatch rules': show 'Route to Agent', so which agent answers a number is a dropdown, not a carrier ticket. Click 'Cancel'.
5. Click 'Dispatch rules', then 'Create new dispatch rule'. Explain Rule type 'Individual' (each caller gets a private room), click 'Add agent' to show Agent name, Deployment and Dispatch metadata, then the 'Trunks' tab under Inbound routing. Ask: 'Do different numbers or brands need different agents or context?'
6. Click the 'JSON editor' tab: the same config is code you can manage from the CLI or API. Click 'Cancel'.
7. Click 'SIP trunks', then 'Create new trunk': keep your own carrier and numbers; show Allowed addresses, 'Optional settings' (SRTP, headers, Krisp), and flip to 'Outbound' for credentials. Click 'Cancel'. Ask: 'Would you start on a LiveKit number for the pilot, or point your existing numbers here?'
8. Proof and depth: DTMF, warm transfer to a human with context, voicemail detection on outbound, Twilio and WhatsApp connectors; telli runs 30,000+ calls a day across 400+ SIP trunks on LiveKit.
9. Close: 'Same agent on the web and on the phone, live in minutes.' Next step: pick the first line (e.g. after-hours), rent or connect one number, and route it to the pilot agent this week.
